html:
Louis Delgres was a colonel of mixed race born in Martinique who led the resistance in Guadeloupe in 1802 against the army sent by Napoleon to restore slavery.

When General Richepance landed in May 1802, Delgres issued a proclamation to the world saying the people would resist. After weeks of fighting he and several hundred followers, cornered at Matouba, blew themselves up rather than surrender, crying "live free or die".

Slavery was restored in Guadeloupe in July 1802 and lasted until 1848. Thousands of people were killed or deported. Long forgotten in France, Delgres was honoured with a plaque in the Pantheon in 1998, and Guadeloupe remembers him and the rebel woman Solitude as heroes, alongside Schoelcher and the earlier abolition under Victor Hugues.
sum: Louis Delgres was a colonel of mixed race born in Martinique who led the resistance in Guadeloupe in 1802 against the army sent by Napoleon to restore slavery.
